audits.text:
## generic_mosaic_occlusion_gen1

**Reproduced query-rotation teaching defect; default ordered tasks remain valid;
audit target left unchanged.** The audited generator SHA-256 is
`e53beb04caccbee084359cdd0988d385c758a5a8bdcee786be8dfd78d96a40e0`
and its declared rule hash is `6e414ea28b65`.

I generated 40 tasks in each of the easy, medium, and hard bands. All 120 tasks
generated successfully and all 120 passed `self_check_task`. I then combined
each task's materialized train/test pairs, held out every pair once as query,
and applied the generator's own `lesson_identifiable` hook to the remaining
demonstrations. Of 549 rotations, 109 were ambiguous. The first counterexample
is easy seed 0: with two train and two test pairs, holding out pair 0 removes the
only vertical-only recovery witness; each of the remaining three pairs has zero
`vertical_only` cells, so a horizontal-only rule is still compatible with every
demonstration.

This is conditional on downstream assembly: the generator's documented original
ordering deliberately puts complementary witnesses in its first two training
pairs and passes its own ordered self-check. It becomes a data defect only when
a pipeline permits arbitrary query rotation or reorders pairs while assuming
identifiability is preserved. The complete generated counterexample, support
counts, task, source hashes, command, and denominator are retained in
`checks/audit/generic_mosaic_occlusion_gen1/rotation_probe.json`; the executable
probe is `checks/audit/generic_mosaic_occlusion_gen1/rotation_probe.py`.
No patch was made because this was an audit-only target.
